We need to create a test class for the method ema(int) of NumericIndicator. Use JUnit5 (JUnit Jupiter) and Mockito. Should test that NumericIndicator.ema returns a NumericIndicator wrapping EMAIndicator correctly. Use existing test style as reference. Need to set up a BarSeries, ClosePriceIndicator, then NumericIndicator.of(cp1).ema(3) returns NumericIndicator whose delegate is EMAIndicator. Verify class type and maybe values.

We need to initialize fields in setupBeforeAll or setupBeforeEach. Use MockBarSeries? In original tests they used MockBarSeries with numFunction injection. In this new test, we can use a simple MockBarSeries from same package. However we need to provide numFunction; the test class template does not have constructor injection. We can create a static Function<Number, Num> using a default number provider like DecimalNum? In ta4j library, there is a DefaultNum? Usually they use DecimalNum::valueOf. Could use org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum. Let's import that.

Simplify: Use a real BarSeries (MockBarSeries) with series of numbers. We'll create a static BarSeries series; a ClosePriceIndicator cp; then test.

Test cases:

- ema returns NumericIndicator with delegate of type EMAIndicator.
- The underlying EMAIndicator computes correct values: compare emaIndicator.getValue(i) with NumericIndicator.ema(barCount).getValue(i). Use assertNumEquals.

Need assertNumEquals method from TestUtils. Could import static org.ta4j.core.TestUtils.assertNumEquals; but that class may be package-private? In original test they used static import. We'll include import.

Also we need to test that calling ema on NumericIndicator created from some other indicator (e.g., ADXIndicator) works.

But focus on method.

Implementation:

class fields: static Function<Number, Num> numFunction = DecimalNum::valueOf; static BarSeries series; static ClosePriceIndicator cp; static NumericIndicator numericIndicator;

In @BeforeAll we can create series using MockBarSeries(numFunction, ...). However MockBarSeries constructor requires Function<Number,Num> and varargs of numbers. We'll replicate.

Set up series with some numbers.

In @BeforeEach maybe not needed.

Test method: @Test void emaCreatesCorrectIndicator().

Implementation: NumericIndicator emaNumeric = numericIndicator.ema(3); assertNotNull(emaNumeric); assertEquals(EMAIndicator.class, emaNumeric.delegate().getClass());

Also verify values: EMAIndicator ema = new EMAIndicator(cp,3); for some indices compare values.

Use assertNumEquals.

Add imports.

Make sure to not use private fields.

All good.
